title: TUI: each prompt keystroke re-registers keymap layers (~15 ms JS per key)

judge.reasoning:
The issue identifies a specific root cause in opencode's own code: several prompt keymap layers in packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx compute an eager `enabled` boolean from per-keystroke state (store.prompt.text, cursorVersion()), so every keystroke re-registers ~6 layers and triggers every useKeymapSelector/useShortcuts memo. The issue's own benchmark shows the lazy-`enabled` change dropping p50 from ~15 ms to ~4 ms.

Patch A implements exactly that fix: it converts each layer's `enabled` to a thunk evaluated on demand, removes the cursorVersion signal and its two setters (so cursor/content changes no longer invalidate the layer factories), introduces a hasText memo so the stash and prompt.clear layers only change when the prompt flips between empty and non-empty, and makes the shell-mode ctrl+c command read hasText too. This is consistent with the existing convention already used for command-level `enabled` (e.g. `enabled: () => store.prompt.text === ""`). It also adds a test that subscribes to the keymap's `state` event, types, moves the cursor, and deletes, asserting zero re-registrations — a test that would fail before the change and pass after — plus regression tests that the cursor-position-dependent `!` shell-mode and backspace-exits-shell behaviors still work without the cursorVersion signal, which is the main behavioral risk of removing it. The bun.lock libc churn is lockfile noise and is ignored per the ground rules.

Patch B only bumps @opentui/core, @opentui/keymap and @opentui/solid from 0.8.0 to 0.8.1 (plus the plugin peer range). Nothing in the diff or the issue indicates that 0.8.1 addresses layer re-registration or selector cost, and the issue states the cause lives in opencode's prompt code, which Patch B leaves untouched. Even if the new keymap version happened to cheapen re-registration, the eager `enabled` evaluation and per-keystroke cursorVersion bumps would remain, so at best it masks the symptom; judged on what is in front of me, it has no demonstrated connection to the fix and adds no tests.

On correctness and tests Patch A is clearly stronger; on scope it is focused on the issue; on craft it matches surrounding conventions and documents the hasText memo's purpose. Patch A wins.

issue_md:
### Description

Every keystroke in the TUI prompt costs ~15 ms of JS before anything is drawn. strace shows the main thread on CPU for the whole interval from reading the key to writing the screen, and a JS sampling profile puts about half of it in `useKeymapSelector` memos.

Cause: several prompt keymap layers compute an eager `enabled` boolean from per-keystroke state inside their `Keymap.createLayer` factory, in `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx`:

- the `prompt.clear` layer reads `store.prompt.text`
- the `!` shell-mode, backspace-exits-shell and history ↑/↓ layers read `cursorVersion()`, which is bumped on every content and cursor change
- the `stashCommands` memo reads `!!store.prompt.text` and returns a new array, so its layer re-registers too

So each key unregisters and re-registers about 6 layers. The keymap emits `state`, and every `useKeymapSelector` memo recomputes, including one `useShortcuts()` memo per caller, each of which rebuilds a formatted Map of every registered command (`context/keymap.tsx`).

Time from a key written to the TUI's PTY to its first output byte (60 keys, fresh session, three interleaved rounds):

| build | p50 ms | p90 ms |
|---|---|---|
| v2.2.1 release | 15.9 · 14.4 · 14.7 | 23.8 · 18.4 · 18.8 |
| v2.2.1 built from source | 15.9 · 14.2 · 18.7 | 21.8 · 17.5 · 24.3 |
| same + lazy `enabled` (PR) | 3.8 · 3.6 · 3.9 | 5.8 · 4.4 · 7.1 |

It doesn't depend on session size. The code is unchanged in v2.2.4 and on `dev`.

### Plugins

none (reproduced with an empty config)

### OpenCode version

2.2.1 (same code in 2.2.4 and dev)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `opencode serve` and attach the TUI to a session on a PTY you control.
2. Write single printable characters to the PTY ~200 ms apart (never submit).
3. Time each write to the TUI's next output byte: ~15 ms p50. A shell on the same PTY echoes in <1 ms.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 (x86_64, 8 vCPU)

### Terminal

PTY driven by a test harness; also felt over ssh in iTerm2

diff --git a/packages/tui/test/prompt-keymap-layers.test.tsx b/packages/tui/test/prompt-keymap-layers.test.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..e355673311
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/tui/test/prompt-keymap-layers.test.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,125 @@
+import { TextareaRenderable } from "@opentui/core"
+import * as opentuiKeymap from "@opentui/keymap/opentui"
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, expect, mock, test } from "bun:test"
+import { takeDraft } from "../src/component/prompt/draft-stash"
+import { createAppFixture } from "./fixture/app"
+
+type OpenTuiKeymap = ReturnType<typeof opentuiKeymap.createDefaultOpenTuiKeymap>
+
+// Captures the app's keymap so the test can watch layer re-registrations. The module mock lasts
+// for the whole test process, so it only captures while this file's tests run.
+const keymaps: OpenTuiKeymap[] = []
+let capturing = false
+const createDefaultOpenTuiKeymap = opentuiKeymap.createDefaultOpenTuiKeymap
+mock.module("@opentui/keymap/opentui", () => ({
+  ...opentuiKeymap,
+  createDefaultOpenTuiKeymap: (...args: Parameters<typeof createDefaultOpenTuiKeymap>) => {
+    const keymap = createDefaultOpenTuiKeymap(...args)
+    if (capturing) keymaps.push(keymap)
+    return keymap
+  },
+}))
+
+type Fixture = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createAppFixture>>
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  // Other app tests can leave a home draft in the process-wide stash.
+  takeDraft(undefined)
+  capturing = true
+})
+
+afterEach(() => {
+  capturing = false
+  keymaps.length = 0
+})
+
+async function open() {
+  const setup = await createAppFixture({ config: { animations: false } })
+  await setup.ready
+  await setup.waitForFrame((frame) => frame.includes("commands"))
+  const prompt = setup.renderer.currentFocusedEditor
+  if (!(prompt instanceof TextareaRenderable)) throw new Error("expected the focused prompt textarea")
+  const keymap = keymaps.at(-1)
+  if (!keymap) throw new Error("expected the app keymap")
+  return { setup, prompt, keymap }
+}
+
+async function settle(setup: Fixture) {
+  await setup.renderOnce()
+  await Bun.sleep(10)
+  await setup.renderOnce()
+}
+
+test("typing and moving the cursor in the prompt does not re-register keymap layers", async () => {
+  const { setup, prompt, keymap } = await open()
+  await using _ = setup
+  let changes = 0
+  const off = keymap.on("state", () => changes++)
+  try {
+    // Let the app's async startup finish registering its layers before counting.
+    await settle(setup)
+    await Bun.sleep(200)
+    await settle(setup)
+    changes = 0
+
+    await setup.mockInput.typeText("hello")
+    await settle(setup)
+    setup.mockInput.pressArrow("left")
+    setup.mockInput.pressArrow("left")
+    await settle(setup)
+    setup.mockInput.pressBackspace()
+    await settle(setup)
+    await setup.mockInput.typeText("p")
+    await settle(setup)
+
+    expect(prompt.plainText).toBe("heplo")
+    expect(changes).toBe(0)
+  } finally {
+    off()
+  }
+})
+
+test("! enters shell mode only at the start of the prompt and backspace there leaves it", async () => {
+  const { setup, prompt } = await open()
+  await using _ = setup
+
+  await setup.mockInput.typeText("a!")
+  await settle(setup)
+  expect(prompt.plainText).toBe("a!")
+  expect(setup.captureCharFrame()).not.toContain("Shell")
+
+  setup.mockInput.pressBackspace()
+  setup.mockInput.pressBackspace()
+  await settle(setup)
+  expect(prompt.plainText).toBe("")
+  await setup.mockInput.typeText("!")
+  await setup.waitForFrame((frame) => frame.includes("Shell"))
+  expect(prompt.plainText).toBe("")
+
+  await setup.mockInput.typeText("ls")
+  await settle(setup)
+  setup.mockInput.pressBackspace()
+  await settle(setup)
+  // Backspace away from the start edits the command and stays in shell mode.
+  expect(prompt.plainText).toBe("l")
+  expect(setup.captureCharFrame()).toContain("Shell")
+
+  setup.mockInput.pressBackspace()
+  await settle(setup)
+  expect(prompt.plainText).toBe("")
+  expect(setup.captureCharFrame()).toContain("Shell")
+  setup.mockInput.pressBackspace()
+  await setup.waitForFrame((frame) => !frame.includes("Shell"))
+})
+
+test("ctrl+c clears typed prompt text", async () => {
+  const { setup, prompt } = await open()
+  await using _ = setup
+
+  await setup.mockInput.typeText("draft text")
+  await settle(setup)
+  expect(prompt.plainText).toBe("draft text")
+  setup.mockInput.pressCtrlC()
+  await settle(setup)
+  expect(prompt.plainText).toBe("")
+})

title: [FEATURE]: Expose Claude Agent plan usage (rate_limit_event) to plugins

judge.reasoning: The source changes are functionally identical: both patches remember the most recent `rate_limit_event` in the stream converter and attach it as `providerMetadata[claude-agent].rateLimit` on both finish parts (tool-call boundary and final result), which is exactly the issue's proposal and surfaces as `native.rateLimit` on `session.step.ended`. B additionally shallow-copies the info per finish, a minor defensive nicety, and its comment names the `native.rateLimit` surface. Independent tests were MISSING on all trees, so the patches' own tests carry the weight. A adds a single test: the first tool-step finish carries the recorded rate limit, and a text result with no event has undefined metadata. B adds three: a full-replay check on a text recording that the finish equals the recorded info and that utilization windows pass through unchanged; a tool-step check that steps before any report carry nothing while later ones carry the latest; and a synthetic test that a second `rate_limit_event` replaces the first. That last case directly exercises the issue's stated requirement ('the latest rate_limit_info'), which A never verifies. All of these would fail before the change and pass after. On scope, B's diff carries an unrelated bun.lock churn stripping `libc` fields across many optional native packages; that looks like a tooling artifact rather than intent and the ground rules say lockfiles are not to be judged, but it is noise that should not be merged as-is. Weighing correctness as equal, B's materially better test coverage of the 'latest' semantics outweighs the lockfile noise, so B is the better fix.

issue_md:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Expose Claude Agent plan usage to plugins.

Claude Code sends a `rate_limit_event` SDK message with utilization and reset times for the 5-hour and weekly windows. The Claude Agent provider only uses it to word limit errors in `claude-agent-error.ts`, and plugins never see it.

Today a plugin that shows Claude subscription usage has to poll `api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage`, which is rate limited, and read Claude Code's OAuth token to do it. The provider's design says OpenCode never reads those tokens. ChatGPT sign-ins don't have this problem: the backend streams a `codex.rate_limits` frame with each response, which plugins can read through the `experimental.ws.receive` hook.

Proposal: attach the latest `rate_limit_info` to the step's finish provider metadata, so it shows up as `native.rateLimit` on `session.step.ended`. That uses the existing event and needs no new API. I have a small PR ready.

title: [FEATURE]: Extensible Markdown code-block actions for GUI plugins

judge.reasoning:
Patch A implements exactly what the issue asks: a `CodeBlockAction` registry whose actions declare applicability (`languages`, `when`), receive code, language, completion state and session, support accessible title, icon, `enabled`/`busy` predicates plus automatic busy while `run` is pending, and disappear when the plugin's items leave the host. It refactors Copy onto the same `MarkdownCodeAction` mechanism (one `createCodeActions` root renders contributed actions then Copy through the same `CodeActionButton`), preserving Copy's behavior, labels and 'Copied' state, and keeps the per-block cost to an empty-list memo when nothing is registered. It adds focused tests covering language filtering, busy/disabled while pending, plugin withdrawal, throwing predicates, and session capture at click time. The independent tests confirm A passes all seven issue-derived scenarios.

Patch B diverges from the ask in several ways. It leaves Copy hardcoded (`createCopyButton` untouched) and bolts a separate `markdown-code-actions` slot in front of it, so Copy is not refactored onto the action mechanism. Its `CodeBlockProps` has no completion state and `CodeBlockAction` has no disabled/busy support or `when` predicate, which is why the independent tests for completion state and busy state fail (FAIL-EXC) on B. Most significantly, B adds a whole `CodeBlock` renderer registry that replaces highlighted code with plugin UI, which the issue explicitly says to avoid ('Keep the API focused on actions rather than replacing Markdown rendering'); that redesign drives most of B's complexity (`decorateCode`, `codeMounts`, redecorate passes, provider toggling in `ui.tsx`) and most of its Playwright test coverage, adding risk unrelated to the request. A's surviving lockfile noise is ignored per the ground rules. On correctness, tests, scope and craft, A is the better fix.

issue_md:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Let built-in and third-party GUI plugins contribute actions alongside **Copy** on fenced code blocks in assistant messages.

Today, Copy is hardcoded in the Markdown renderer, and GUI plugins have no supported way to add code-block buttons. This prevents features such as **Run in terminal** from being implemented within the terminal plugin without app-specific wiring or DOM manipulation.

**Proposed scope:**
- Add a code-block action registry to the GUI plugin API.
- Let actions declare when they apply—for example, only to particular languages—and receive the original code, language, completion state, and owning session.
- Support accessible labels, icons, and disabled/busy states, with contributions removed when their plugin unloads.
- Refactor Copy onto the same action mechanism, preserving its existing behavior and availability without requiring a plugin.

Keep the API focused on actions rather than replacing Markdown rendering, and avoid adding per-row work when no plugin actions are registered.

**Motivating use case:** the built-in terminal plugin could contribute **Run in terminal** for shell blocks. That feature is already requested in #60875; execution semantics and terminal selection would be reviewed separately. This proposal does not enable command execution itself.

Related: #54126 proposed extensible fenced-code rendering for the TUI. This request concerns additive actions in the desktop/web Markdown UI.

Would this be an acceptable extension point before an implementation is started?

@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+import type { CodeBlock, CodeBlockAction, SessionRef } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
+import type { MarkdownCodeAction, MarkdownCodeBlock } from "@opencode/session-ui/context/markdown"
+import type { Item } from "./host"
+
+/**
+ * The Markdown code actions of plugin CodeBlockAction contributions, in `order`. A predicate that throws reports the
+ * error through `fail` and answers false (hidden, disabled, not busy), so one plugin's broken action never breaks a
+ * message.
+ */
+export function markdownCodeActions(input: {
+  items: readonly Item<CodeBlockAction>[]
+  session: () => SessionRef
+  fail: (plugin: string, error: Error) => void
+  /** Reuses each item's action while the item is unchanged, so keyed buttons keep their busy state across updates. */
+  cache?: WeakMap<Item<CodeBlockAction>, MarkdownCodeAction>
+}): readonly MarkdownCodeAction[] {
+  return input.items
+    .toSorted((a, b) => (a.value.order ?? 0) - (b.value.order ?? 0))
+    .map((item) => {
+      const cached = input.cache?.get(item)
+
+      if (cached) return cached
+      const action = markdownCodeAction(item, input.session, input.fail)
+      input.cache?.set(item, action)
+
+      return action
+    })
+}
+
+function markdownCodeAction(
+  item: Item<CodeBlockAction>,
+  session: () => SessionRef,
+  fail: (plugin: string, error: Error) => void,
+): MarkdownCodeAction {
+  const action = item.value
+  const languages = action.languages?.map((language) => language.toLowerCase())
+
+  const block = (current: MarkdownCodeBlock): CodeBlock => ({
+    get code() {
+      return current.code
+    },
+    get language() {
+      return current.language
+    },
+    get complete() {
+      return current.complete
+    },
+    get session() {
+      return session()
+    },
+  })
+
+  const ask = (check: ((block: CodeBlock) => boolean) | undefined, current: MarkdownCodeBlock, otherwise: boolean) => {
+    if (!check) return otherwise
+
+    try {
+      return check(block(current))
+    } catch (error) {
+      fail(item.plugin, error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)))
+
+      return false
+    }
+  }
+
+  return {
+    id: item.key,
+    get label() {
+      return action.title
+    },
+    get icon() {
+      return action.icon
+    },
+    applies: (current) => (!languages || languages.includes(current.language)) && ask(action.when, current, true),
+    enabled: (current) => ask(action.enabled, current, true),
+    busy: (current) => ask(action.busy, current, false),
+    // The block as it is at the click, so a run that awaits still acts on the session and code the user chose.
+    run: (current) =>
+      action.run({
+        code: current.code,
+        language: current.language,
+        complete: current.complete,
+        session: session(),
+      }),
+  }
+}

+import { afterEach, expect, mock, test } from "bun:test"
+import { createRequire } from "node:module"
+import { createSignal } from "solid-js"
+import type { CodeBlock, CodeBlockAction, SessionRef } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
+import type { Item } from "@/runtime/plugin/host"
+import type { MarkdownCodeAction } from "@opencode/session-ui/context/markdown"
+import { markdownCodeActions } from "@/runtime/plugin/code-block-actions"
+
+// Bun does not compile Solid JSX. Compile the code block actions and the UI they render with the same presets as Vite.
+const require = createRequire(import.meta.url)
+
+const solid = createRequire(require.resolve("vite-plugin-solid"))
+
+const { transformSync } = solid("@babel/core")
+
+// This file runs with --isolate. Replace the shared hyperscript preload so Solid owns the buttons' reactivity.
+Bun.plugin.clearAll()
+
+Bun.plugin({
+  name: "markdown-code-actions-solid",
+  setup(build) {
+    build.onLoad({ filter: /[\\/]packages[\\/](ui|session-ui)[\\/]src[\\/].*\.tsx$/ }, async (args) => ({
+      contents: transformSync(await Bun.file(args.path).text(), {
+        filename: args.path,
+        presets: [solid.resolve("babel-preset-solid"), solid.resolve("@babel/preset-typescript")],
+      }).code,
+      loader: "js",
+    }))
+  },
+})
+
+const { createCodeActions, disposeCodeActions, setCodeActionLabels, updateCodeActions } = await import(
+  "../../session-ui/src/components/markdown-code-actions"
+)
+
+const labels = { copy: "Copy", copied: "Copied" }
+
+/** The routed session; the code under test only hands it to the plugin. */
+function sessionRef(key: string) {
+  // SAFETY: the code under test reads nothing from the session; it passes it to the action, which reads only `key`.
+  // oxlint-disable-next-line anti-slop/no-chained-type-assertions -- see SAFETY above
+  return { key } as unknown as SessionRef
+}
+
+function item(plugin: string, value: CodeBlockAction): Item<CodeBlockAction> {
+  return { key: `${plugin}:${value.id}`, plugin, value }
+}
+
+/** A fenced code block as Markdown renders it: the wrapper, its `pre > code`, then the actions. */
+function block(input: {
+  code: string
+  language: string | undefined
+  complete: boolean
+  items: () => readonly Item<CodeBlockAction>[]
+  session?: () => SessionRef
+  fail?: (plugin: string, error: Error) => void
+  cache?: WeakMap<Item<CodeBlockAction>, MarkdownCodeAction>
+}) {
+  const wrapper = document.createElement("div")
+  wrapper.dataset.component = "markdown-code"
+  const pre = document.createElement("pre")
+  const code = document.createElement("code")
+  code.textContent = input.code
+  pre.append(code)
+  wrapper.append(pre)
+  document.body.append(wrapper)
+
+  const actions = () =>
+    markdownCodeActions({
+      items: input.items(),
+      session: input.session ?? (() => sessionRef("server\nsession")),
+      fail: input.fail ?? (() => undefined),
+      cache: input.cache,
+    })
+
+  wrapper.append(createCodeActions({ labels, language: input.language, complete: input.complete, actions }))
+
+  return { wrapper, code }
+}
+
+const buttons = (root: Element) =>
+  Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>("button")).map((button) => button.getAttribute("aria-label"))
+
+const button = (root: Element, label: string) => {
+  const found = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>("button")).find(
+    (candidate) => candidate.getAttribute("aria-label") === label,
+  )
+
+  if (!found) throw new Error(`no ${label} button among ${buttons(root).join(", ")}`)
+
+  return found
+}
+
+const settle = () => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0))
+
+afterEach(() => {
+  disposeCodeActions(document.body)
+  document.body.replaceChildren()
+})
+
+test("without contributed actions a code block shows only Copy, which copies the block's code", async () => {
+  const writeText = mock(async (_text: string) => undefined)
+  Object.defineProperty(navigator, "clipboard", { configurable: true, value: { writeText } })
+  const { wrapper } = block({ code: "echo hi\n", language: "bash", complete: true, items: () => [] })
+
+  expect(buttons(wrapper)).toEqual(["Copy"])
+
+  button(wrapper, "Copy").click()
+  await settle()
+
+  expect(writeText.mock.calls).toEqual([["echo hi\n"]])
+  expect(buttons(wrapper)).toEqual(["Copied"])
+
+  setCodeActionLabels(document.body, { copy: "Kopieren", copied: "Kopiert" })
+
+  expect(buttons(wrapper)).toEqual(["Kopiert"])
+})
+
+test("a plugin action lists before Copy only on the languages it names and receives the block", async () => {
+  const runs: { code: string; language: string; complete: boolean; session: string }[] = []
+
+  const run = item("terminal", {
+    id: "run",
+    title: "Run in terminal",
+    icon: "console",
+    languages: ["Bash", "sh"],
+    enabled: (current) => current.complete,
+    run: (current: CodeBlock) => {
+      runs.push({
+        code: current.code,
+        language: current.language,
+        complete: current.complete,
+        session: current.session.key,
+      })
+    },
+  })
+
+  const shell = block({ code: "echo hi\n", language: "BASH", complete: false, items: () => [run] })
+  const typescript = block({ code: "const a = 1\n", language: "ts", complete: true, items: () => [run] })
+  const plain = block({ code: "plain\n", language: undefined, complete: true, items: () => [run] })
+
+  expect(buttons(shell.wrapper)).toEqual(["Run in terminal", "Copy"])
+  expect(buttons(typescript.wrapper)).toEqual(["Copy"])
+  expect(buttons(plain.wrapper)).toEqual(["Copy"])
+
+  // Streaming: disabled until the block completes.
+  expect(button(shell.wrapper, "Run in terminal").disabled).toBe(true)
+  shell.code.textContent = "echo hi\necho done\n"
+  updateCodeActions(shell.wrapper, { language: "bash", complete: true })
+  expect(button(shell.wrapper, "Run in terminal").disabled).toBe(false)
+
+  button(shell.wrapper, "Run in terminal").click()
+  await settle()
+
+  expect(runs).toEqual([{ code: "echo hi\necho done\n", language: "bash", complete: true, session: "server\nsession" }])
+})
+
+test("an action is busy while its run is pending, and leaves every block when its plugin withdraws it", async () => {
+  const [items, setItems] = createSignal<readonly Item<CodeBlockAction>[]>([])
+  const pending: (() => void)[] = []
+
+  const first = block({ code: "ls\n", language: "sh", complete: true, items })
+  const second = block({ code: "pwd\n", language: "sh", complete: true, items })
+
+  expect(buttons(first.wrapper)).toEqual(["Copy"])
+
+  setItems([
+    item("terminal", {
+      id: "run",
+      title: "Run in terminal",
+      icon: "console",
+      order: 1,
+      run: () => new Promise<void>((resolve) => pending.push(resolve)),
+    }),
+    item("notes", { id: "save", title: "Save snippet", icon: "plus", run: () => undefined }),
+  ])
+
+  expect(buttons(first.wrapper)).toEqual(["Save snippet", "Run in terminal", "Copy"])
+  expect(buttons(second.wrapper)).toEqual(["Save snippet", "Run in terminal", "Copy"])
+
+  button(first.wrapper, "Run in terminal").click()
+  await settle()
+
+  expect(button(first.wrapper, "Run in terminal").getAttribute("aria-busy")).toBe("true")
+  expect(button(first.wrapper, "Run in terminal").disabled).toBe(true)
+  expect(button(second.wrapper, "Run in terminal").getAttribute("aria-busy")).toBeNull()
+
+  pending.forEach((resolve) => resolve())
+  await settle()
+
+  expect(button(first.wrapper, "Run in terminal").getAttribute("aria-busy")).toBeNull()
+  expect(button(first.wrapper, "Run in terminal").disabled).toBe(false)
+
+  setItems([])
+
+  expect(buttons(first.wrapper)).toEqual(["Copy"])
+  expect(buttons(second.wrapper)).toEqual(["Copy"])
+})
+

+  const error = new Error("broken when")
+

+    code: "echo hi\n",
+    language: "bash",
+    complete: true,
+    fail: (plugin, cause) => failures.push(`${plugin}: ${cause.message}`),
+    items: () => [
+      item("broken", {
+        id: "run",
+        title: "Broken",
+        icon: "console",
+        when: () => {
+          throw error

+      }),
+    ],
+  })
+
+  expect(buttons(wrapper)).toEqual(["Copy"])
+  expect(failures).toEqual(["broken: broken when"])
+})
+
+test("an action reads the session it runs in when the user clicks", async () => {
+  const [session, setSession] = createSignal(sessionRef("server\nfirst"))
+  const seen: string[] = []
+
+  const { wrapper } = block({
+    code: "echo hi\n",
+    language: "bash",
+    complete: true,
+    session,
+    items: () => [
+      item("terminal", {
+        id: "run",
+        title: "Run in terminal",
+        icon: "console",
+        run: (current) => void seen.push(current.session.key),
+      }),
+    ],
+  })
+
+  setSession(sessionRef("server\nsecond"))
+  button(wrapper, "Run in terminal").click()
+  await settle()
+
+  expect(seen).toEqual(["server\nsecond"])
+})
+
+test("an action runs against the session the user clicked in, even after the route changes mid-run", async () => {
+  const [session, setSession] = createSignal(sessionRef("server\nfirst"))
+  const seen: string[] = []
+  const pending: (() => void)[] = []
+
+  const { wrapper } = block({
+    code: "echo hi\n",
+    language: "bash",
+    complete: true,
+    session,
+    items: () => [
+      item("terminal", {
+        id: "run",
+        title: "Run in terminal",
+        icon: "console",
+        run: async (current) => {
+          await new Promise<void>((resolve) => pending.push(resolve))
+          seen.push(current.session.key)
+        },
+      }),
+    ],
+  })
+
+  button(wrapper, "Run in terminal").click()
+  setSession(sessionRef("server\nsecond"))
+  pending.forEach((resolve) => resolve())
+  await settle()
+
+  expect(seen).toEqual(["server\nfirst"])
+})
+
+test("a pending action stays busy when another plugin contributes an action", async () => {
+  const pending: (() => void)[] = []
+
+  const run = item("terminal", {
+    id: "run",
+    title: "Run in terminal",
+    icon: "console",
+    run: () => new Promise<void>((resolve) => pending.push(resolve)),

+

+

+})

+import { createMemo, createSignal, For, onCleanup, Show, type Accessor, type Setter } from "solid-js"
+import { render } from "solid-js/web"
+import { Icon } from "@opencode/ui/icon"
+import { IconButton } from "@opencode/ui/icon-button"
+import { Loader } from "@opencode/ui/loader"
+import { Tooltip } from "@opencode/ui/tooltip"
+import type { MarkdownCodeAction, MarkdownCodeBlock } from "../context/markdown"
+
+export type CopyLabels = {
+  copy: string
+  copied: string
+}
+
+type CodeActionsState = {
+  setLabels: Setter<CopyLabels>
+  setLanguage: Setter<string>
+  setComplete: Setter<boolean>
+  dispose: () => void
+}
+
+const slot = "markdown-code-actions"
+
+const codeActionsState = new WeakMap<HTMLElement, CodeActionsState>()
+
+const doneDuration = 2000
+
+const noActions: readonly MarkdownCodeAction[] = []
+
+/** The language a code action sees: the fence's, lowercased, or `text` when it names none. */
+function codeActionLanguage(language: string | undefined) {
+  return language?.toLowerCase() || "text"
+}
+
+/**
+ * The actions of one code block: the provider's actions that apply to it, then Copy. The host goes inside the block's
+ * `markdown-code` wrapper, after its `pre`, which is where the block's code is read from.
+ */
+export function createCodeActions(input: {
+  labels: CopyLabels
+  language: string | undefined
+  complete: boolean
+  actions: Accessor<readonly MarkdownCodeAction[] | undefined>
+}) {
+  const host = document.createElement("div")
+  host.setAttribute("data-slot", slot)
+
+  const state: Partial<CodeActionsState> = {}
+
+  const dispose = render(() => {
+    const [labels, setLabels] = createSignal(input.labels, { equals: false })
+    const [language, setLanguage] = createSignal(codeActionLanguage(input.language))

+### Code block actions
+
+`CodeBlockAction` adds a button beside Copy on the fenced code blocks of a session's Markdown: the timeline's messages
+and `ctx.ui.Markdown` on the session screen. The host owns the button, its tooltip, and its disabled and busy states.
+Your action says which blocks it applies to and what it does with the block's code:
+
+```ts
+import { CodeBlockAction } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
+
+ctx.add(
+  CodeBlockAction,
+  (): CodeBlockAction => ({
+    id: "run",
+    icon: "console",
+    title: ctx.t("run"),
+    languages: ["bash", "sh", "shell", "zsh"],
+    enabled: (block) => block.complete,
+    run: (block) => runInTerminal(block.session, block.code),
+  }),
+)
+```
+
+- `title` is the button's accessible name and tooltip. `icon` is required.
+- `languages` limits the action to fences that name one of them, compared lowercased. A fence without a language is
+  `text`. Omit `languages` for every block.
+- `when`, `enabled` and `busy` receive the block and run again when its `language` or `complete` changes. `when` hides
+  the action, `enabled` disables it, `busy` shows a spinner. A promise that `run` returns also keeps the button busy
+  until it settles.
+- `block.code` is the code without the fence, as rendered so far; read it in `run`. `block.complete` turns true once
+  the block has finished streaming.
+- `block.session` is the session whose Markdown shows the block.
+- `order` sorts your actions among other plugins' actions, lowest first. Every contributed action lists before Copy.
+- A `when`, `enabled` or `busy` that throws hides or disables only your action and records the error. The host logs a
+  rejected `run`; show the user your own error where they need one.
+
+#### Reference
+
+```ts
+interface CodeBlockAction {
+  id: string
+  title: string
+  icon: IconName
+  order?: number
+  languages?: string[]
+  when?: (block: CodeBlock) => boolean
+  enabled?: (block: CodeBlock) => boolean
+  busy?: (block: CodeBlock) => boolean
+  run(block: CodeBlock): void | Promise<void>
+}
+
+interface CodeBlock {
+  code: string
+  language: string
+  complete: boolean
+  session: SessionRef
+}
+```

+### Code blocks
+
+`CodeBlock` renders the fenced code blocks of the languages you list as your own UI, in place of the highlighted code.
+Use it for content that reads better drawn than as source, such as a ` ```csv ` table or a ` ```latex `
+formula:
+
+```tsx
+import { For } from "solid-js"
+import { CodeBlock } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
+
+ctx.add(CodeBlock, {
+  languages: ["csv"],
+  render: (props) => {
+    const rows = props.code.split("\n").map((line) => line.split(","))
+
+    if (rows.length < 2) return undefined
+
+    return (
+      <table>
+        <tbody>
+          <For each={rows}>
+            {(row) => (
+              <tr>
+                <For each={row}>{(cell) => <td>{cell}</td>}</For>
+              </tr>
+            )}
+          </For>
+        </tbody>
+      </table>
+    )
+  },
+})
+```
+
+- `languages` are compared with the first word of the fence's info string, lowercased: ` ```CSV title="Q3" `
+  matches `csv`. The host resolves no aliases, so list each name you accept.
+- `render` receives the block's `code`, its `language` and the `session` that shows it. Return `undefined` or `null` to
+  keep the highlighted code, for example when the source does not parse.
+- A render that throws records the error under your plugin, and the block shows its code. Your other contributions
+  keep working.
+- When several plugins list a language, the first contributed renders it. Your renderer also replaces the app's own
+  Mermaid diagram when you list `mermaid`.
+
+#### Streaming
+
+The host renders a block only once its closing fence arrives. While the block streams, and in a message that stopped
+mid-block, the user sees the highlighted code; then your UI replaces it in place. Your render never sees half a block.
+
+#### Where it applies
+
+| Surface                                                        | Code block content |
+| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
+| Timeline: assistant text and tool output                       | Yes                |
+| Side panels on the session screen, e.g. the Markdown preview   | Yes                |
+| `ctx.ui.Markdown` rendered on the session screen               | Yes                |
+| `ctx.ui.Code`, and Markdown inside your own `CodeBlock` render | No                 |
+| Settings pages, dialogs and other surfaces off the screen      | No                 |
+
+#### Layout and performance
+
+- Blocks of languages no plugin lists cost nothing; only a block of a listed language renders your UI, and only while
+  its timeline row is on screen.
+- The block grows and shrinks with your UI. Give asynchronous content a minimum height, so the timeline shifts less
+  when it arrives.
+- The block keeps its Copy button, which copies the source, and your `CodeBlockAction` buttons over its top end corner.
+
+### Code block actions
+
+`CodeBlockAction` adds a button beside the Copy button of the code blocks of the languages you list. `run` receives the
+same block a `CodeBlock` render receives:
+
+```ts
+import { CodeBlockAction } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
+
+ctx.add(CodeBlockAction, {
+  id: "run",
+  languages: ["sh", "bash", "shell", "zsh"],
+  icon: "terminal",
+  get title() {
+    return ctx.t("run")
+  },
+  run: (input) => runInTerminal(input.code, input.session),
+})
+```
+
+- The button shows once the block's closing fence arrives, so it never acts on half a command.
+- Buttons reveal with Copy on hover or keyboard focus, before it, in ascending `order`.
+- Read `title` from a getter so it follows the locale.
+- A `run` that throws or rejects is logged under your plugin and changes nothing else.
+
+#### Reference
+
+```ts
+interface CodeBlock {
+  languages: string[]
+  render(props: CodeBlockProps): JSX.Element | undefined
+}
+
+interface CodeBlockAction {
+  id: string
+  languages: string[]
+  icon: IconName
+  title: string
+  order?: number
+  run(input: CodeBlockProps): void | Promise<void>
+}
+
+interface CodeBlockProps {
+  code: string
+  language: string
+  session?: MountedSession
+}
+```

title: [FEATURE]: Make the active session ID easy to copy in Desktop

judge.reasoning:
The issue asks for a one-click way to copy the ID of the session currently being viewed, from the session header or its menu. Patch B does exactly that: it extracts the existing copy-session-ID logic into a reusable `useCopySessionID` hook and `SessionCopyIDMenuItem`, refactors the existing command to use it, and adds the menu item to the session header's location card, the timeline's session options menu, the tab context menu, the sidebar inbox, project session rows, and home session rows. The active session's ID is now reachable from the header and multiple menus with one click, with success/failure toasts, and the hook has unit tests covering desktop clipboard, browser fallback, and failure reporting. Scope is tight and consistent with surrounding menu conventions (sits next to Export / SessionReadMenuItem).

Patch A instead builds a right-click context menu on session *references* inside transcript markdown and composer mentions (Copy Session ID / Copy Session Title / Open Session), plus a session-ID cell in the debug bar plugin. Neither surfaces the active session's ID in the session header or its options menu: the reference menu only applies to IDs that happen to appear in message text or mentions, and the debug bar is an opt-in developer plugin, not the normal Desktop session view. The patch also carries substantial unrelated churn: it changes how session references render (prepending '@' to titles), rewrites their CSS, alters copy-to-clipboard behaviour for selections containing references, and adds a new lookup state machine for fetching titles of unloaded sessions. That is a broader redesign that adds risk and does not address the issue's core ask. Its tests are reasonable for what it builds, but they test the reference menu and lookup machine, not the requested header/menu action.

The independent tests are MISSING on all trees, so they provide no signal. On correctness relative to the issue, scope, and relevance of tests, Patch B is clearly the better fix.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

When I use OpenCode Desktop, I often need another session to summarize a session's work or continue that work. I need a quick way to get the ID of the session I'm currently viewing, without having to search for it elsewhere.

Please make the active session ID easy to find and copy from the Desktop session view, for example through a one-click copy action in the session header or menu. This would make cross-session workflows much faster.

diff --git a/packages/app/src/session/session-copy-id-menu-item.test.ts b/packages/app/src/session/session-copy-id-menu-item.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..3a85f8e546
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/app/src/session/session-copy-id-menu-item.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+import { beforeEach, describe, expect, mock, test } from "bun:test"
+import { createRoot } from "solid-js"
+
+const writes: string[] = []
+const toasts: Record<string, unknown>[] = []
+let failWrite: unknown
+let desktopClipboard = true
+
+mock.module("@/runtime/i18n/language", () => ({ useLanguage: () => ({ t: (key: string) => key }) }))
+
+mock.module("@/runtime/platform/platform", () => ({
+  usePlatform: () => ({
+    platform: "desktop",
+    writeClipboardText: desktopClipboard
+      ? async (text: string) => {
+          if (failWrite) throw failWrite
+          writes.push(`desktop:${text}`)
+        }
+      : undefined,
+  }),
+}))
+
+mock.module("@/shell/notifications/toast", () => ({
+  showToast: (options: Record<string, unknown>) => {
+    toasts.push(options)
+  },
+}))
+
+const { useCopySessionID } = await import("./session-copy-id-menu-item")
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  writes.length = 0
+  toasts.length = 0
+  failWrite = undefined
+  desktopClipboard = true
+})
+
+function copier() {
+  return createRoot((dispose) => {
+    const copy = useCopySessionID()
+    dispose()
+
+    return copy
+  })
+}
+
+describe("copy session id", () => {
+  test("puts the session's id on the desktop clipboard and confirms it", async () => {
+    await copier()("ses_abc123")
+
+    expect(writes).toEqual(["desktop:ses_abc123"])
+    expect(toasts).toEqual([
+      { variant: "success", icon: "circle-check", title: "common.copied", description: "ses_abc123" },
+    ])
+  })
+
+  test("falls back to the browser clipboard when the platform has none", async () => {
+    desktopClipboard = false
+    const original = navigator.clipboard.writeText
+    navigator.clipboard.writeText = async (text: string) => {
+      writes.push(`browser:${text}`)
+    }
+
+    try {
+      await copier()("ses_web")
+    } finally {
+      navigator.clipboard.writeText = original
+    }
+
+    expect(writes).toEqual(["browser:ses_web"])
+    expect(toasts.at(-1)).toMatchObject({ variant: "success", description: "ses_web" })
+  })
+
+  test("reports a clipboard failure instead of claiming the copy", async () => {
+    failWrite = new Error("clipboard denied")
+
+    await copier()("ses_abc123")
+
+    expect(writes).toEqual([])
+    expect(toasts).toEqual([
+      { variant: "error", title: "toast.session.copyID.failed.title", description: "clipboard denied" },
+    ])
+  })
+
+  test("describes a failure that carries no message", async () => {
+    failWrite = "denied"
+
+    await copier()("ses_abc123")
+
+    expect(toasts).toEqual([
+      {
+        variant: "error",
+        title: "toast.session.copyID.failed.title",
+        description: "toast.session.copyID.failed.description",
+      },
+    ])
+  })
+})
diff --git a/packages/app/src/session/session-copy-id-menu-item.tsx b/packages/app/src/session/session-copy-id-menu-item.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..52d8fb61d6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/app/src/session/session-copy-id-menu-item.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+import { Show } from "solid-js"
+import { Icon } from "@opencode/ui/icon"
+import { Menu } from "@opencode/ui/menu"
+import { useLanguage } from "@/runtime/i18n/language"
+import { usePlatform } from "@/runtime/platform/platform"
+import { showToast } from "@/shell/notifications/toast"
+
+/** Copies a session's id to the clipboard and reports the outcome in a toast. */
+export function useCopySessionID() {
+  const language = useLanguage()
+  const platform = usePlatform()
+
+  return async (sessionID: string) => {
+    try {
+      await (platform.writeClipboardText?.(sessionID) ?? navigator.clipboard.writeText(sessionID))
+      showToast({
+        variant: "success",
+        icon: "circle-check",
+        title: language.t("common.copied"),
+        description: sessionID,
+      })
+    } catch (err) {
+      showToast({
+        variant: "error",
+        title: language.t("toast.session.copyID.failed.title"),
+        description: err instanceof Error ? err.message : language.t("toast.session.copyID.failed.description"),
+      })
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+export function SessionCopyIDMenuItem(props: { sessionID: string | undefined; icon?: boolean }) {
+  const language = useLanguage()
+  const copy = useCopySessionID()
+
+  return (
+    <Menu.Item
+      disabled={!props.sessionID}
+      onSelect={() => {
+        const id = props.sessionID
+
+        if (id) void copy(id)
+      }}
+    >
+      <Show when={props.icon}>
+        <Icon name="outline-copy" class="text-v2-icon-icon-muted" />
+      </Show>
+      {language.t("command.session.copyID")}
+    </Menu.Item>
+  )
+}

+import { Show } from "solid-js"
+import { Portal } from "solid-js/web"
+import { Menu } from "@opencode/ui/menu"
+import { writeClipboard } from "@opencode/session-ui/copy"
+import { useLanguage } from "@/runtime/i18n/language"
+import { usePlatform } from "@/runtime/platform/platform"
+import { useData } from "@/runtime/server/current"
+import { showToast } from "@/shell/notifications/toast"
+
+export type SessionReferenceMenuTarget = { sessionID: string; x: number; y: number }
+
+export function SessionReferenceMenu(props: {
+  target: SessionReferenceMenuTarget | undefined
+  currentSessionID: string | undefined
+  onOpenSession: (sessionID: string) => void
+  onClose: () => void
+}) {
+  const language = useLanguage()
+  const platform = usePlatform()
+  const data = useData()
+
+  const title = () => {
+    const session = props.target ? data.session.get(props.target.sessionID) : undefined
+
+    return session && !session.time.archived ? session.title || undefined : undefined
+  }
+
+  const copy = async (text: string, failure: { title: string; description: string }) => {
+    try {
+      const written = platform.writeClipboardText
+        ? await platform.writeClipboardText(text).then(() => true)
+        : await writeClipboard(text)
+
+      if (!written) throw new Error(failure.description)
+      showToast({ variant: "success", icon: "circle-check", title: language.t("common.copied"), description: text })
+    } catch (err) {
+      showToast({
+        variant: "error",
+        title: failure.title,
+        description: err instanceof Error ? err.message : failure.description,
+      })
+    }
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <Menu
+      modal={false}
+      placement="bottom-start"
+      gutter={2}
+      open={!!props.target}
+      onOpenChange={(open) => {
+        if (!open) props.onClose()
+      }}
+    >
+      {/* Portaled so a transformed ancestor never offsets the fixed trigger. */}
+      <Portal>
+        <Menu.Trigger
+          as="span"
+          aria-hidden="true"
+          disabled
+          class="pointer-events-none fixed size-px"
+          style={{ left: `${props.target?.x ?? 0}px`, top: `${props.target?.y ?? 0}px` }}
+        />
+      </Portal>
+      <Menu.Portal>
+        <Menu.Content onCloseAutoFocus={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
+          <Show when={props.target?.sessionID}>
+            {(sessionID) => (
+              <>
+                <Show when={sessionID() !== props.currentSessionID}>
+                  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => props.onOpenSession(sessionID())}>
+                    {language.t("session.reference.open")}
+                  </Menu.Item>
+                </Show>
+                <Menu.Item
+                  onSelect={() =>
+                    void copy(sessionID(), {
+                      title: language.t("toast.session.copyID.failed.title"),
+                      description: language.t("toast.session.copyID.failed.description"),
+                    })
+                  }
+                >
+                  {language.t("command.session.copyID")}
+                </Menu.Item>
+                <Show when={title()}>
+                  {(value) => (
+                    <Menu.Item
+                      onSelect={() =>
+                        void copy(value(), {
+                          title: language.t("session.reference.copyTitle.failed"),
+                          description: language.t("common.requestFailed"),
+                        })
+                      }
+                    >
+                      {language.t("session.reference.copyTitle")}
+                    </Menu.Item>
+                  )}
+                </Show>
+              </>
+            )}
+          </Show>
+        </Menu.Content>
+      </Menu.Portal>
+    </Menu>
+  )
+}

+import type { SessionInfo } from "@opencode/client/promise"
+import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test"
+import {
+  createSessionReferenceLookupState,
+  transitionSessionReferenceLookup,
+  type SessionReferenceLookupEvent,
+  type SessionReferenceLookupState,
+} from "./session-reference-lookup-machine"
+
+const ID = "ses_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop"
+
+function info(archived?: number): SessionInfo {
+  return {
+    id: ID,
+    projectID: "proj",
+    cost: 0,
+    tokens: { input: 0, output: 0, reasoning: 0, cache: { read: 0, write: 0 } },
+    location: { directory: "/project" },
+    title: "Linked",
+    time: { created: 1, updated: 1, archived },
+  }
+}
+
+function replay(events: readonly SessionReferenceLookupEvent[], state = createSessionReferenceLookupState()) {
+  return events.reduce<SessionReferenceLookupState>(
+    (current, event) => transitionSessionReferenceLookup(current, event).state,
+    state,
+  )
+}
+
+describe("transitionSessionReferenceLookup", () => {
+  test("looks an unknown ID up once and remembers the session it finds", () => {
+    const requested = transitionSessionReferenceLookup(createSessionReferenceLookupState(), {
+      type: "requested",
+      sessionID: ID,
+    })
+
+    expect(requested.effects).toEqual([{ type: "fetch", sessionID: ID, attempt: 1 }])
+
+    // Markdown asks again on every render while the request runs, and after it settles.
+    const repeated = transitionSessionReferenceLookup(requested.state, { type: "requested", sessionID: ID })
+    expect(repeated.state).toBe(requested.state)
+    expect(repeated.effects).toEqual([])
+
+    const session = info()
+
+    const resolved = transitionSessionReferenceLookup(requested.state, {
+      type: "resolved",
+      sessionID: ID,
+      attempt: 1,
+      session,
+    })
+
+    expect(resolved.effects).toEqual([{ type: "remember", session }])
+    expect(transitionSessionReferenceLookup(resolved.state, { type: "requested", sessionID: ID }).effects).toEqual([])
+  })
+
+  test("a missing, failed or archived session is not asked for again and is not remembered", () => {
+    const missing = transitionSessionReferenceLookup(replay([{ type: "requested", sessionID: ID }]), {
+      type: "unavailable",
+      sessionID: ID,
+      attempt: 1,
+    })
+
+    expect(missing.effects).toEqual([])
+    expect(transitionSessionReferenceLookup(missing.state, { type: "requested", sessionID: ID }).effects).toEqual([])
+
+    const archived = transitionSessionReferenceLookup(replay([{ type: "requested", sessionID: ID }]), {
+      type: "resolved",
+      sessionID: ID,
+      attempt: 1,
+      session: info(5),
+    })
+
+    expect(archived.effects).toEqual([])
+  })
+
+  test("a server change aborts earlier lookups, ignores their answers and asks again", () => {
+    const changed = transitionSessionReferenceLookup(replay([{ type: "requested", sessionID: ID }]), {
+      type: "server.changed",
+    })
+
+    expect(changed.effects).toEqual([{ type: "abort-all" }])
+
+    const stale = transitionSessionReferenceLookup(changed.state, {
+      type: "resolved",
+      sessionID: ID,
+      attempt: 1,
+      session: info(),
+    })
+
+    expect(stale.state).toBe(changed.state)
+    expect(stale.effects).toEqual([])
+
+    expect(transitionSessionReferenceLookup(changed.state, { type: "requested", sessionID: ID }).effects).toEqual([
+      { type: "fetch", sessionID: ID, attempt: 2 },
+    ])
+  })
+
+  test("disposing aborts lookups and ignores later answers", () => {
+    const disposed = transitionSessionReferenceLookup(replay([{ type: "requested", sessionID: ID }]), {
+      type: "disposed",
+    })
+
+    expect(disposed.effects).toEqual([{ type: "abort-all" }])
+    expect(
+      transitionSessionReferenceLookup(disposed.state, { type: "resolved", sessionID: ID, attempt: 1, session: info() })
+        .effects,
+    ).toEqual([])
+  })
+})

@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+import type { SessionInfo } from "@opencode/client/promise"
+
+/**
+ * Lookups of sessions the transcript references but this window has not loaded. Each ID is looked up once per
+ * provider: `pending` while the request runs, `settled` after it, whether the session was found, missing, archived or
+ * the request failed. A found session goes into the session cache, which is what renders the reference's title.
+ */
+export type SessionReferenceLookupState =
+  | {
+      readonly status: "active"
+      readonly attempt: number
+      readonly entries: ReadonlyMap<string, { readonly status: "pending"; readonly attempt: number } | SettledEntry>
+    }
+  | { readonly status: "disposed" }
+
+type SettledEntry = { readonly status: "settled" }
+
+export type SessionReferenceLookupEvent =
+  | { readonly type: "requested"; readonly sessionID: string }
+  | { readonly type: "resolved"; readonly sessionID: string; readonly attempt: number; readonly session: SessionInfo }
+  /** Not found, archived, or the request failed: the reference stays its raw ID. */
+  | { readonly type: "unavailable"; readonly sessionID: string; readonly attempt: number }
+  /** The provider moved to another server, so every earlier answer is for the wrong one. */
+  | { readonly type: "server.changed" }
+  | { readonly type: "disposed" }
+
+export type SessionReferenceLookupEffect =
+  | { readonly type: "fetch"; readonly sessionID: string; readonly attempt: number }
+  | { readonly type: "remember"; readonly session: SessionInfo }
+  | { readonly type: "abort-all" }
+
+export type SessionReferenceLookupTransition = {
+  readonly state: SessionReferenceLookupState
+  readonly effects: readonly SessionReferenceLookupEffect[]
+}
+
+const NONE: readonly SessionReferenceLookupEffect[] = []
+
+const SETTLED: SettledEntry = Object.freeze({ status: "settled" })
+
+export function createSessionReferenceLookupState(): SessionReferenceLookupState {
+  return { status: "active", attempt: 0, entries: new Map() }
+}
+
+export function transitionSessionReferenceLookup(
+  state: SessionReferenceLookupState,
+  event: SessionReferenceLookupEvent,
+): SessionReferenceLookupTransition {
+  if (state.status === "disposed") return { state, effects: NONE }
+
+  if (event.type === "disposed") return { state: { status: "disposed" }, effects: [{ type: "abort-all" }] }
+
+  if (event.type === "server.changed") {
+    if (state.entries.size === 0) return { state, effects: NONE }
+
+    return { state: { status: "active", attempt: state.attempt, entries: new Map() }, effects: [{ type: "abort-all" }] }
+  }
+
+  if (event.type === "requested") {
+    if (state.entries.has(event.sessionID)) return { state, effects: NONE }
+    const attempt = state.attempt + 1
+
+    return {
+      state: {
+        status: "active",
+        attempt,
+        entries: new Map(state.entries).set(event.sessionID, { status: "pending", attempt }),
+      },
+      effects: [{ type: "fetch", sessionID: event.sessionID, attempt }],
+    }
+  }
+
+  const entry = state.entries.get(event.sessionID)
+
+  if (entry?.status !== "pending" || entry.attempt !== event.attempt) return { state, effects: NONE }
+
+  const next: SessionReferenceLookupState = {
+    status: "active",
+    attempt: state.attempt,
+    entries: new Map(state.entries).set(event.sessionID, SETTLED),
+  }
+
+  if (event.type === "unavailable" || event.session.time.archived) return { state: next, effects: NONE }
+
+  return { state: next, effects: [{ type: "remember", session: event.session }] }
+}

title: patch: case-only rename deletes the file on case-insensitive filesystems

judge.reasoning:
Both patches detect a case-only move and switch from write-then-remove to rename-then-write (or write-then-rename), so both fix the reported `same.txt` -> `Same.txt` deletion on a case-insensitive volume.

Correctness: Patch A gates its new path on the source being a regular file and on `stat(moveTarget)` succeeding. That works for the issue's exact scenario, but it deliberately routes symlink sources back to write-then-remove; on a case-insensitive filesystem `write(Same.txt)` then writes *through* the symlink `same.txt` into its target and the subsequent `remove` deletes the link, so A's own comment ('leaves their target alone') is wrong precisely in the environment the issue is about, and the existing test suite shows the project cares about not clobbering symlink targets. Patch B's `caseAlias` path renames first, stats the renamed entry, removes it if it is a symlink, then writes, which is correct for files and symlinks on both case-sensitive and case-insensitive hosts, refuses to rename onto an existing directory, and creates the destination directory when the case-differing parent does not exist on a case-sensitive host. B also normalises (NFC) before folding, which matters on macOS.

Tests: A's two new tests run on a case-sensitive host through the unchanged code path (`stat(Same.txt)` fails there), so they pass on the base commit and only exercise the fix on macOS/Windows. B adds a `fold` layer to the existing mocked environment that simulates case-insensitive resolution and case-only rename, so its primary test actually reproduces the issue on Linux and fails before the fix; it also covers the case-sensitive path, a differently-cased directory, the directory-collision rejection, and the symlink case. The independent tests were all MISSING, so they provide no signal either way.

Scope/craft: B carries unrelated `bun.lock` churn (dropping `libc`/`hasInstallScript` fields across many platform packages), which looks like a tooling artefact and would need reverting; that is a real mark against it, but lockfile noise does not obscure the fix in `patch.ts`. B's fix is longer, but the error messages follow the existing `fail(...)` convention and each step is explained. On balance B resolves the issue more completely (symlinks, both host types) and is the only one whose tests demonstrate the bug and the fix on the CI host.

issue_md:
### Description

On a case-insensitive filesystem (the macOS and Windows defaults), a patch that only changes the case of a file name deletes the file.

`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/patch.ts:185` treats the hunk as a move because `same.txt` and `Same.txt` are different strings. That check comes from #59197, which fixed moves onto the exact same path (`./same.txt`), but it doesn't catch a case change. The apply step then writes `Same.txt`, which overwrites `same.txt` in place, and removes `same.txt`, which is the same file (`patch.ts:233-239`). The tool then fails with:

```
Failed to read <dir>/Same.txt: file does not exist. Completed before failure: Same.txt
```

On a case-sensitive filesystem the same patch renames the file correctly.

The `v1` branch has the same write-then-remove in `apply_patch.ts` and no guard even for the exact same path (#45310 was closed, but its fix #45316 was not merged).

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

2.2.7 (dev at edfe6510d)

### Steps to reproduce

1. On a case-insensitive filesystem, create `same.txt` containing `before`.
2. Run the `patch` tool with:
   ```
   *** Begin Patch
   *** Update File: same.txt
   *** Move to: Same.txt
   @@
   -before
   +after
   *** End Patch
   ```
3. The directory is now empty and the tool returns the error above. Expected: `Same.txt` containing `after`.

I reproduced it with a test added to `packages/core/test/tool-patch.test.ts` (using `withTempTool` and `executeTool`), run with `TMPDIR` on a vfat mount. The same test passes on ext4.

### Screenshot

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS and Windows (any case-insensitive volume); reproduced on Linux with a vfat mount

### Terminal

_No response_
